name: kernl
description: Coding agents in VS Code: Deep Agents with your own model key, or Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode, in parallel worktree workspaces. Every edit, command, and browser action waits for your approval.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode the agent can only read files: no edits, commands, browser, or MCP tools. The project's AGENTS.md, .kernl rules, and .kernl agents are not loaded, and settings that run programs, skip approvals, or choose endpoints come only from your user settings.

commands.title: Ask kernl about this file or selection

kernl.provider.markdownDescription:
Model provider for the kernl agent: `anthropic`, `openai`, `google`, `deepseek`, `openai-compatible`, or `custom:<id>` for an entry in `#kernl.customProviders#`. Easiest: the model chip in the panel, or **kernl: Manage providers**.

**Stored data:** [Clear stored keys](command:kernl.clearKeys) (API keys for every provider and CLI agent) · [Delete conversations and checkpoints](command:kernl.clearHistory) (your files are not changed). Both ask first.

kernl.model.markdownDescription: Model id, e.g. `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `gpt-5.6`, `gemini-3.1-pro`, `deepseek-flash`, or a local model name. Empty uses `deepseek-flash` for `deepseek` and the entry's model for a custom provider.

kernl.modelOptions.markdownDescription:
Optional model parameters for Deep Agents:

- `temperature`: 0 to 2 (0 to 1 for anthropic)
- `maxOutputTokens`: the longest reply
- `reasoningEffort`: `low`, `medium`, or `high`. OpenAI-style providers get reasoning effort, anthropic gets extended thinking (2048 / 8192 / 24576 tokens; not with `temperature`), google gets a thinking level. Not supported for deepseek.

A value a provider can't take is named in the panel instead of being dropped. `#kernl.modelProfiles#` overrides these per model.

contextWindow.markdownDescription: The model's context window in tokens. Deep Agents compacts the conversation at 85% of it; without it, at 170k tokens for models it doesn't know.

kernl.modelProfiles.markdownDescription:
Options per model, over `#kernl.modelOptions#`. Keys are `provider/model` (e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`, `custom:gateway/team/model`) or `*` for every model; the model's own entry wins. The thinking chip writes `reasoningEffort` here (`off` turns off an effort set by a broader entry).

```json
{ "*": { "contextWindow": 200000 }, "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5": { "reasoningEffort": "high", "contextWindow": 1000000 } }
```

protocol.markdownDescription: The API the service speaks: `openai` (`/chat/completions`) or `anthropic` (`/v1/messages`; `baseUrl` is the part before `/v1`).

headers.markdownDescription: Headers sent with every request, e.g. a team id. Not for secrets: values here are plain settings.

secretHeaders.markdownDescription: Names of headers whose values are kept in VS Code's secret storage (set them with **kernl: Set API key**). A provider with one needs no API key.

kernl.customProviders.markdownDescription:
OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible services, each selectable as `kernl.provider` `custom:<id>`. Keys and secret header values are stored with **kernl: Add custom provider** or **kernl: Set API key**, never here.

User settings only: a workspace can't point your keys at another server.

kernl.baseUrl.markdownDescription:
Base URL for the `openai-compatible` provider, e.g. `http://localhost:11434/v1` for Ollama.

User settings only.

kernl.sequentialThinking.markdownDescription: Give the kernl agent a built-in sequential-thinking tool for complex tasks: numbered thoughts it can revise or branch, shown in the conversation. (Built in, adapted from the Model Context Protocol reference server; no MCP server runs.)

enumDescriptions: Open while the agent thinks, then collapse to one line (click to reopen)
kernl.thinkingDisplay.markdownDescription: How the agent's thinking shows in the panel (any agent that shares it: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and kernl's own agent with DeepSeek, or Claude with `#kernl.modelOptions#` `reasoningEffort` set).

kernl.approvals.allow.markdownDescription:
Actions that run **without a card**. An allow never matches a command with shell operators (`;`, `&&`, `|`, `>`, `$(`...), so `npm test && rm x` still asks.

Rules: `run(command *)`, `edit(glob)` (edits and new files), `delete(glob)`, `read(glob)` (only sensitive files like `.env` ask to be read), `tool(name *)` for browser and MCP tools. Globs are relative to the workspace: `**` spans folders, `*` stays in one. A trailing ` *` in `run(...)` also matches the bare command.

Deny beats ask beats allow; no match asks. Applies to Deep Agents; CLI agents use their own settings. User settings only.

kernl.approvals.ask.markdownDescription:
Actions that always ask, even when an allow rule also matches. Example: `edit(src/migrations/**)`.

Rules: `run(command *)`, `edit(glob)` (edits and new files), `delete(glob)`, `read(glob)` (only sensitive files like `.env` ask to be read), `tool(name *)` for browser and MCP tools. Globs are relative to the workspace: `**` spans folders, `*` stays in one. A trailing ` *` in `run(...)` also matches the bare command.

Deny beats ask beats allow; no match asks. Applies to Deep Agents; CLI agents use their own settings. User settings only.

kernl.approvals.deny.markdownDescription:
Actions refused **without a card**; the transcript names the rule. Deny matches the command as written, so it isn't a security boundary: `rm` behind another command or script still reaches a card, never runs on its own.

Rules: `run(command *)`, `edit(glob)` (edits and new files), `delete(glob)`, `read(glob)` (only sensitive files like `.env` ask to be read), `tool(name *)` for browser and MCP tools. Globs are relative to the workspace: `**` spans folders, `*` stays in one. A trailing ` *` in `run(...)` also matches the bare command.

Deny beats ask beats allow; no match asks. Applies to Deep Agents; CLI agents use their own settings. User settings only.

kernl.commandAllowList.markdownDescription:
Commands that run without asking. Exact match only; any command with shell operators always asks.

User settings only.
kernl.commandAllowList.markdownDeprecationMessage: Use `#kernl.approvals.allow#` with `run(...)` rules. Entries here still work as exact matches.

kernl.harness.markdownDescription:
Agent for the main workspace (the panel's agent picker sets this). Worktree workspaces pick their own.

- `deepagents`: the kernl agent with your own model keys
- `deepagents:<name>`: a named agent from `.kernl/agents/` or `.claude/agents/` (project or your home folder)
- `claude-code`: Claude Code (your installed CLI and login), Manual mode
- `codex`: Codex (experimental), Read-only mode
- `opencode`: OpenCode (your installed CLI); every edit, command, and fetch asks

kernl.agentCommands.markdownDescription:
Override how a CLI agent is launched: `{ "claude-code" | "codex" | "opencode": { "command": string, "args"?: string[], "env"?: object } }`. Ask-mode forcing still applies.

User settings only: a workspace can't choose what program runs.

kernl.sessions.importFromAgents.markdownDescription: List Claude Code's, Codex's, and OpenCode's own sessions for the folder in **Conversations** (started in a terminal or another app), and open them in kernl with their history. kernl asks each ready agent for its list (ACP `session/list`); it doesn't read their files.

kernl.tabs.max.markdownDescription: How many tabs a workspace can have open (its first tab included); `0` means no limit. At the limit, a new tab closes the tab shown longest ago that isn't working; its conversation stays in **Conversations**.

kernl.sources.claudeCode.skills.markdownDescription: kernl's own agent uses your Claude Code skills: `~/.claude/skills` (including synced ones) and, in trusted workspaces, the project's `.claude/skills`. Claude Code itself always loads them.

kernl.sources.claudeCode.commands.markdownDescription: Claude Code slash commands (`~/.claude/commands`, the project's `.claude/commands`) become skills for kernl's own agent.

kernl.sources.claudeCode.agents.markdownDescription: Claude Code subagents (`~/.claude/agents`, the project's `.claude/agents`) become named kernl agents.

kernl.sources.claudeCode.instructions.markdownDescription: kernl's own agent follows `CLAUDE.md` (yours in `~/.claude`, and the project's) and the project's `.claude/rules`.

kernl.sources.claudeCode.mcpServers.markdownDescription: kernl's own agent connects to the MCP servers in `~/.claude.json` and, in trusted workspaces, the project's `.mcp.json` (each project server asks once before it first starts). Servers that sign in with OAuth are listed as skipped: use them in Claude Code.

kernl.sources.claudeCode.plugins.markdownDescription: kernl's own agent uses your enabled Claude Code plugins: their skills, commands, agents, and MCP servers. Plugin hooks and workflows run only in Claude Code.

kernl.sources.codex.skills.markdownDescription: kernl's own agent uses Codex skills: `~/.agents/skills` and, in trusted workspaces, the project's `.agents/skills`.

kernl.sources.codex.mcpServers.markdownDescription: kernl's own agent connects to the MCP servers in `~/.codex/config.toml`.

kernl.sources.opencode.skills.markdownDescription: kernl's own agent uses OpenCode skills: `~/.config/opencode/skills` and, in trusted workspaces, the project's `.opencode/skills`.

kernl.sources.opencode.mcpServers.markdownDescription: kernl's own agent connects to the MCP servers in OpenCode's config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` or `.jsonc`; in trusted workspaces also the project's, each project server asking once).

kernl.sources.opencode.instructions.markdownDescription: kernl's own agent follows the instruction files listed in OpenCode's config (`instructions`).

kernl.mcpServers.markdownDescription:
kernl's own MCP servers: `{ name: { command, args?, env? } | { url, headers? } }`. Every MCP tool call asks first. Servers from Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode are added by the Sources settings; on the same name, these win.

User settings only: a workspace can't start programs through this setting.

kernl.mcp.toolTimeoutSeconds.markdownDescription: How long an MCP tool call may take before kernl stops waiting and reports it.

enumDescriptions: Claude Code and OpenCode run their commands in VS Code's terminal through kernl, with kernl's approvals. Codex keeps its own shell; its output is shown in the terminal.
The agents keep their own shells. kernl shows a copy of the output where the agent provides one (Claude Code, Codex).
kernl.terminal.cliAgents.markdownDescription: Where CLI agents run shell commands.

kernl.terminal.outputLimit.markdownDescription: Characters of a command's output kept for the agent (the start and the end are kept; the middle is cut).

kernl.browser.cliAgents.markdownDescription: Give Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode kernl's browser tools, so they can open, read, and click pages in VS Code's integrated browser (every action that changes a page asks first).

kernl.browser.timeoutSeconds.markdownDescription: How long one browser action may take before it fails (the next action reconnects).

kernl.connections.pollSeconds.markdownDescription: While the kernl panel is visible, check the agents' logins again every this many seconds (Claude Code keeps its login in the macOS keychain, which kernl can't watch). `0` checks only at startup, when you come back to VS Code, and when a login file or key changes.

kernl.connections.checkKeys.markdownDescription: Check stored API keys with the provider's model list (`GET /models`: no tokens spent) when a key changes and when the Connections view opens.

kernl.replaceChatButton.markdownDescription: Hide VS Code's chat button in the Command Center and use kernl's instead: the kernl button in the editor toolbar right below it, the `kernl` status bar item, and `Ctrl+Alt+K`. This sets VS Code's `#chat.agentsControl.enabled#` to `hidden` in your user settings; turning this off puts back what was there. (VS Code doesn't let extensions place a button in the Command Center itself.)

kernl.statusBar.show.markdownDescription: Show `kernl` in the status bar: it opens the kernl menu, and warns when a login, key, or MCP server needs you.
